slides.heading: Using type()
slides.body: Using type() is part of Variables and Primitive Data Types. This short lesson gives you a practical Python idea you can understand, try, and reuse in simple programs.

slides.heading: Core Idea: Using type()
slides.body: The type() function tells you what kind of data a value has. It helps beginners check whether a value is an integer, float, string, or boolean.

slides.heading: Real-World Analogy
slides.body: type() is like asking a librarian what category a book belongs to before you borrow it.

slides.heading: Key Rule
slides.body: Use clear variable names and match the data type to the kind of value you need to store.

slides.heading: Try It Yourself!
slides.prompt: Use type() to check the data type of a variable named score.

coding_challenge.prompt_text: Create a variable named amount with the value 25.5 and print its type.
coding_challenge.hint_text: Use the idea from the lesson. Keep the code short, readable, and correctly indented.
